title: Exact capacity of the independent binary deletion channel
statement: Determine the Shannon capacity C(d) in bits per input bit of the binary channel that independently deletes each input bit with probability d∈(0,1), preserves the order of surviving bits and does not reveal deletion locations, without feedback.
source_locator: SRC-FORMAL-318, Sections 1.2, 2 and 14.3; SRC-IMPACT-009 README; Khodaiemehr-Feng-Duman v2, Theorems 1-2, Lemma 8, Section VI-C and Table IV
status_basis: The inspected September 2026 run-length paper retains the exact-capacity question and reports additional lower bounds. These results and the previously indexed enclosure remain source-reported computations, not independently replayed project benchmarks.
plain_summary: When missing bits leave no position markers, even the maximum reliable information rate is unknown. The half-deletion case provides a fixed parameter at which stronger bounds would be useful.
assumptions: Each binary input symbol is deleted independently with fixed probability d; surviving symbols retain their order.
Use Shannon capacity without feedback, normalized per input bit, and vanishing error as block length grows.
Allow arbitrary input distributions when claiming an upper bound on capacity. A bound restricted to one source family is not a general converse.
scope: The target is the exact no-feedback capacity function C(d). The d=1/2 case is a bounded entry point; an improved bound there is partial progress. Optimizing a restricted source family gives achievable rates, not exact capacity.
target: Determine capacity, or establish a rigorously stronger achievable-rate or converse bound at an explicitly fixed deletion probability.
success_criteria: State the exact parameter, normalization, inequalities and theorem connecting the certificate to unrestricted channel capacity.
Compare against precise source endpoints, rather than claiming novelty from rounded displayed decimals.
Provide an independently reproducible proof or numerical certificate with controlled arithmetic, including every required input.
known_results: SRC-FORMAL-318 Table 1 reports 0.114540<=C(1/2)<=0.130162 bits per input bit, rounded outward. These are claimed certified enclosures, not ordinary floating-point estimates; the project has not replayed them.
The source distinguishes an achievable lower endpoint from a midpoint estimate, and leaves source and converse optimization open.
SRC-IMPACT-009 lists portable checks but says the full large-input collection is not yet downloadable in full. Those checks do not rerun the numerical inequalities.

Khodaiemehr, Feng and Duman v2 report interval-enclosed run-length lower bounds after correcting the VTR chain penalty. Table IV gives stronger high-deletion rates, while its half-deletion lower endpoint remains below the enclosure recorded above. No computation was replayed here.
prerequisites: Rigorous numerical bounds and exact certificate arithmetic
significance: A sharper capacity benchmark would clarify limits of communication with synchronization loss. Practical encoders and realistic DNA-storage models require additional analysis.
